tags.label: Route isolation
tags.description: Separate forms, sources, or workflow routes need separate handling before outputs are promoted.
applies_when: Assets mention route classification, routing, form handling, or route-specific evaluation.
does_not_apply_when: The task has only one stable source form and no route-dependent behavior.
tags.risk_if_misapplied: May overcomplicate a simple workflow and delay useful work.

tags.label: Chunking
tags.description: Text, code, or corpus assets are split into reusable chunks, packets, or spans.
applies_when: Assets mention chunks, spans, context packets, token windows, or source segmentation.
does_not_apply_when: The asset is not content-like or does not need retrieval/comparison.
tags.risk_if_misapplied: May treat arbitrary file boundaries as meaningful evidence.

tags.label: Gold promotion
tags.description: Expected outputs, gold cases, or reviewed examples are promoted through a gate.
applies_when: Tests, fixtures, review packets, or docs mention gold, golden, reviewed examples, or promotion decisions.
does_not_apply_when: Examples are exploratory, unreviewed, or intentionally temporary.
tags.risk_if_misapplied: May freeze bad examples as truth before review.

tags.label: Schema contract
tags.description: Schemas, validators, type contracts, or structured data constraints govern behavior.
applies_when: Assets include JSON Schema, validators, typed contracts, or schema-conformance tests.
does_not_apply_when: The work is exploratory prose or does not create structured records.
tags.risk_if_misapplied: May force premature structure before the domain is understood.

tags.label: Source authority
tags.description: A source repository, source corpus, or authority file retains control over meaning.
applies_when: The lesson touches source truth, canon, provenance, or generated candidate evidence.
does_not_apply_when: The work is purely local generated reporting with no authority implications.
tags.risk_if_misapplied: May block harmless derived reporting or overstate authority concerns.

tags.label: Human gate
tags.description: A human decision is required before promotion, mutation, merge, or default behavior change.
applies_when: Assets mention review gates, approval, preflight, postflight, or explicit human decisions.
does_not_apply_when: The action is generated-only reporting or a reversible local fixture.
tags.risk_if_misapplied: May unnecessarily slow safe deterministic reporting.

tags.label: Duplicate or variant
tags.description: Assets appear repeated, copied, near-duplicate, variant, or delta-worthy.
applies_when: Same names, paths, hashes, chunks, or roles recur across repos, worktrees, or archives.
does_not_apply_when: Similar names refer to intentionally independent modules.
tags.risk_if_misapplied: May collapse useful variants or overstate sameness.

tags.label: Temp fixture noise
tags.description: Evidence comes from temp folders, test scaffolds, synthetic repos, or generated fixtures.
applies_when: Paths include pytest temp roots, tmp/temp directories, fixture repos, or generated test workspaces.
does_not_apply_when: The path is an active source repository or curated archive.
tags.risk_if_misapplied: May promote synthetic failures or fixture patterns as production lessons.

tags.label: Dependency ordering
tags.description: The order of build steps, validators, schemas, gates, or data sources likely affected outcome quality.
applies_when: Failures appear before tests, validators, schemas, review gates, or source manifests are added.
does_not_apply_when: Evidence does not include a sequence or dependency relationship.
tags.risk_if_misapplied: May invent an order from coincidental co-occurrence.

tags.label: Late stabilizer
tags.description: A test, validator, schema, gate, or review packet appears late after repeated failure signals.
applies_when: A stabilizing artifact appears after error, failure, revert, or drift evidence.
does_not_apply_when: The stabilizer was present from the start or the sequence is unknown.
tags.risk_if_misapplied: May blame missing gates when the real cause was changing requirements.

tags.label: Repeated failure
tags.description: Similar failures, TODOs, reverts, or error terms recur across attempts or history.
applies_when: Failure-like terms recur in multiple assets, commits, tests, or worktrees.
does_not_apply_when: Only one isolated failure signal exists.
tags.risk_if_misapplied: May overweight common words like error or fail without task context.

tags.label: Counterfactual sequence
tags.description: A candidate lesson proposes a better order for future similar work.
applies_when: Evidence supports a plausible 'do X before Y next time' ordering.
does_not_apply_when: The order is a preference without failure, timing, or dependency evidence.
tags.risk_if_misapplied: May turn one project's recovery path into a rigid universal process.

tags.label: Score methodology
tags.description: A calculated score, grade, confidence, threshold, lift, risk, or similarity value needs an explicit formula and methodology version.
applies_when: The task creates, changes, interprets, or uses a calculated value for review, ranking, graph edges, or roadmap evidence.
does_not_apply_when: The work only stores raw observations and no calculated value is introduced or used.
tags.risk_if_misapplied: May add unnecessary ceremony to simple raw evidence, or hide formulas when applied too weakly.

tags.label: Calibration
tags.description: Human or measured review is comparing generated heuristics against observed usefulness, correctness, safety, or future value.
applies_when: The task reviews labels, thresholds, score bands, false positives, false negatives, or weight changes.
does_not_apply_when: The task only generates candidate records without review or measured comparison.
tags.risk_if_misapplied: May imply a score is validated when it is only generated or guessed.

rule: Context tags are candidate routing and safety labels. They help constrain lessons; they do not prove that a lesson applies.
